subject: the small matter of a dog

messages.text:
Dear Luis,

I wonder if I could trouble you for a little help on the afternoon of the 24th.  A friend has asked me to have his dog while he's at a wedding.  I said yes before consulting the basket of cinema tickets in my desk, which I now discover contains a matinee booked in February.  In February I seem to have thought October would take care of itself.

What I need, if you are about, is somebody to sit in the house for the time it takes to watch the film and get back.  The dog is Fig.  She's small, although she makes a noise you'd associate with something much bigger when the post comes.  She should have been out by the time you arrive.  There's no need to take her round Highbury yourself.  You can read, or put something on the television, if I can remember which remote belongs to it.  I expect to be back by five.

Yours,
Hamish Fairweather
five is fine. when would you need me there? could do 2 if i go straight from the shops.

Dear Luis,

Two would be splendid if that's when Fig arrives.  My friend had first said before lunch and now says they may be coming by train, which in his messages appears to mean any time from half past one to three.  I would quite like you to meet her with him here, so she doesn't decide that you've come to take away the sofa.  Her rule is that the sofa is hers unless she is eating.

Hello everyone,

Lenora
